title: History of Toyota | TOYOTA Motor Manufacturing UK
content: toyota-world-banner-range.jpg. # History of Toyota. Toyota's origins lie in the Japanese weaving industry when Sakichi Toyoda invented the world's first automatic loom and, subsequently, set up the Toyoda Spinning and Weaving Company in 1918. This in turn led to the launch of the Company's first ever passenger car in 1936, the Model AA, and in 1937, the Toyota Motor Company was born. Production of Toyota vehicles outside Japan began in 1959 in Brazil and now, besides its own plants, manufacturing subsidiaries and affiliates in Japan, Toyota manufactures Toyota and Lexus brand vehicles and components throughout the world. Look back at the history of Toyota, starting with the birth of founder Sakichi Toyoda. Find out more about the history of Toyota on the Toyota Motor Corporation website. Come directly to the source at our Burnaston state of the art manufacturing facility and learn more about Toyota's approach to manufacturing. At every stage of a vehicle's life, Toyota strives to protect the environment through reducing energy use and minimising waste.

title: History of Toyota - Wikipedia
content: # History of Toyota. Replica of the Toyota Model AA, the first production model of Toyota in 1936. The **history of Toyota** started in 1933 with the company being a division of Toyoda Automatic Loom Works devoted to the production of cars under the direction of the founder's son, Kiichiro Toyoda. Toyoda Automatic Loom Works was encouraged to develop automobile production by the Japanese government, which needed domestic vehicle production, due to the war with China. In 1934, the division produced its first Type A Engine, which was used in the first Model A1 passenger car in May 1935 and the G1 truck in August 1935. Production of the Model AA passenger car started in 1936. In 1957, the Crown became the first Japanese car to be exported to the United States and Toyota's American and Brazilian divisions, *Toyota Motor Sales Inc.* and *Toyota do Brasil S.A.*, were also established.
